title: Fermi estimate: value of a public CBAM calculation tool
description: Expected-value estimate for building a public, source-bound CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) calculation tool, conditional on the stated premise that a usable tool causes an additional 10% reduction in global GHG emissions within one year.

words.name: CBAM public calculation tool
words.description: Publicly usable, source-verifiable tool for calculating carbon-border-adjustment obligations, in the zukunft.com sense of numbers bound to word/triple/source chains

words.name: usable
words.description: Tool is technically functional AND adopted at a scale sufficient to plausibly drive the assumed emissions effect (e.g. integrated into EU CBAM reporting workflows or widely used by importers/civil society) — bundles technical completion and adoption

words.name: global GHG emissions 2024
words.description: Total global greenhouse gas emissions, 2024, GtCO2eq, all sectors including LULUCF

words.name: social cost of carbon (SCC)
words.description: EPA 2023 central estimate, 2020 USD per metric ton CO2, 2% near-term discount rate

words.name: causal chain: tool usable -> 10% reduction
words.description: The assumed mechanism: public tool -> supply-chain transparency -> closes carbon-leakage gap -> changes importer behavior -> tightens policy -> global emissions effect. Stated as a premise by the user, NOT independently derived or verified here.

values.note: range 120-340 USD/t depending on discount rate (2.5%/2.0%/1.5%)
values.source: EPA Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Dec 2023

values.note: User-stated premise, taken as given for this model; not derived from an independent causal chain. This is the single largest source of uncertainty in the whole estimate and should be its own decomposed sub-model.
2 developers + 1 trade/carbon-accounting domain expert + 1 policy/legal, 18 months, plus data licensing/verification infrastructure
conditional on technical completion; largest source of adoption uncertainty

formula: EV = P(usable) * (0.10 * global_emissions_2024 * SCC) - build_cost, where P(usable) = P(technical completion) * P(adoption)

result.expected_value_note: One-year, non-compounding effect only, per the stated premise. If the effect is assumed durable/annual, NPV over 10y at 5% discount scales roughly x7.7.
result.sensitivity: Cost-effectiveness case (build_cost vs. EV) is positive even at P(usable) as low as 0.0001 (EV ~110M USD, still >>build_cost). The result is therefore almost entirely determined by v3 (the 10% causal premise), not by cost or adoption probability.

open_questions: Decompose v3 (10% global reduction from one tool becoming usable) into its own causal chain: transparency -> carbon-leakage closure -> importer behavior change -> policy tightening -> measured emissions effect, each with sourced or explicitly assumed sub-values.

Current EU CBAM covers a small fraction of traded goods/sectors (steel, aluminium, cement, fertilizer, electricity, hydrogen) and has no export-rebate symmetry as of 2026 — relevant prior constraint on how large a plausible tool-driven effect could be.
